Batch21 records source/private-fixture implementation and inert production discovery; no live preference setters, configure/Notify/reloads, Lock/inhibition, registration/invocation, location/activation, cache rebuild, application launch, privileged appearance helper or live installation. Of51 final fingerprints47match; cached location drift preceded build, other cache/display drift first observed across interrupted build and first probe; transient shortcut-label drift returned to baseline. runtime_acceptance: For each applicable capability: read current, stage/cancel, apply, observe live effect and persistence, reread, compare KDE, reset/defaults, external edit/conflict, denied/canceled authorization, service/device loss, invalid input, version mismatch, and sign-out/reboot disclosures. Real mutations remain unverified.

next_safe_implementation_groups.scope: Keyboard/shortcuts remainder: edited Exec/name runtime adoption through a verified service/session restart or component-recreation dependency adapter (cache refresh alone does not replace the loaded service); arbitrary individual-action deletion/context activation where applicable; physical geometry for other applicable keyboard models; exhaustive dynamic provider reconciliation and full live acceptance. Batches 11–16 retain bounded preferences, registered globals, common standard bindings, compiled PC-model preview, verified-KWin-6.6.6 layout creation/reload, scheme artifacts/review/drafts, custom application/command management, guarded whole-component context-aware removal and retained import dependencies. Definition registration and binding Apply remain explicit; verified Custom Apply only schedules guarded read-only global Refresh before fresh review and explicit binding staging. Unsupported compositor/layout capabilities remain explicit; LayoutLoopCount stays read-only on Wayland. Real preference writes/reloads, recorder inhibition, physical invocation, command/application launch, edited-command/application adoption and sign-in persistence remain unverified; full installed-KDE completion remains open.

Native pointer and keyboard foundations have bounded conditional-provider fixtures. Preserve unresolved workspace bindings, keyboard accessibility, shortcut/default/conflict behavior and physical-device/live-write acceptance. Batches23–24 migrate Screen Locking, Night Light and Day and Night file work to value-only workers with app-owned jobs, retained service/activity, common target/global canonical/inode reservations and soft progress. Next migrate Power Policy, Appearance, Aero Effects, Aero Theme, Theme Components, Font and Keyboard and adopt shared ownership; preserve native merge/non-CAS, Notify broadcast and sent-call late-execution limits. Font/Keyboard failed-sync cleanup remains in place. See docs/audits/kconfig-sync-lifecycle.md.

Display: mirroring/preferred-mode editing, primary ordering, HDR/color/VRR and remaining provider controls; no invented factory defaults, and real multi-monitor/recovery acceptance remains open. Power: activities/inhibitors/scripts/per-profile performance/charge-health/peripheral controls and mobile-frontend reconciliation. Batches17–18 retain guarded layout/scaling/orientation, capability-driven policies and per-key explicit/default operations with native custom-value domains. Physical effects, native reload adoption and persistence remain unverified; no hardware exclusion is inferred. Batch19 adds conditional Night Light filter/default/preview fixtures. Complete the linked native Day and Night schedule/location forms with privacy, daemon migration, timing validation, source/default differences and real acceptance; inert discovery must not activate or subscribe to KNightTime. Batch20 adds bounded native Day and Night forms, offline map, native forecasts and explicit app-owned one-shot location; actual acquisition/denial, legacy migration, runtime adoption and physical/sign-in acceptance remain open.
Exact AccountsService task adapters; locale provider and full installed accessibility schemas; locking/chrony/Bluetooth/printing with failure and authorization paths.
